analysis.title: Base Metals Comment: Blue Wave, Copper Ripples
key_insights: GS leaves its copper forecast unchanged at $15,400/t in 2027 (13% upside vs. spot) following the midterms, but sees two downside risks: AI-related positioning and US tariffs.

The forecast rests on continued US stockbuilding ahead of potential tariffs, China's scrap shortage and elevated investor positioning. The midterms put the stockbuilding and positioning drivers at risk.

LME copper has fallen about 7% over the past month to $13,588/t, largely on volatility in AI-related equities after the Democratic sweep. GS reads the correction as positioning-driven, not a loosening of fundamentals.

Physical fundamentals remain tight. The Yangshan import premium is at a record high above $200/t, reflecting limited metal availability in China and outside the US, and ex-US inventories are at seasonal lows.

Combined COMEX and LME net length fell to about 9% of open interest last week from about 21% at end-September, below the 16% GS assumes from 2027. At current positioning, GS's model implies 2027 copper averaging about $14,600/t versus the $15,400/t forecast.

Copper has tracked the GS AI Data Center basket since late 2025. Positioning may stay subdued if equity markets price an earlier turn in the AI capex cycle, even while data center construction continues.

Data center moratoria are a delay risk with limited copper demand impact over the next two years. GS economists expect short-lived, conditional moratoria from Democratic governors in Texas, Georgia and Michigan, mainly affecting new projects rather than those under construction.

Capacity under construction is sufficient to meet GS's forecast US data center additions through 2028. If all under-construction Texas capacity were delayed six months, about 50kt of copper demand would shift out of 2027, cutting the 2027 forecast by at most about $100/t to $15,300/t.
Moratorium risk is greater from 2029, when the forecast relies more on projects not yet under construction, though announced high-likelihood projects point to a pipeline well above what GS assumes.

The COMEX-LME spread implies a tariff duty of just 1% for January 2027 and about 6-7% for January 2028, which signals limited near-term tariff expectations and puts the US stockbuilding assumption at risk.

GS assumes about 400kt of US inventory overbuild in 2027. If US stockbuilding stopped altogether, copper would average about $14,500/t in 2027, with further downside if this year's US inventory build flowed back to the rest of the world.

The Democratic sweep does not eliminate tariff risk. The decision is a presidential one under Section 232, and rolling it back through legislation would need bipartisan support, which Democrats may not prioritize for refined copper.

sector_views.rationale: GS keeps a $15,400/t 2027 forecast on tight physical fundamentals, but flags downside from low positioning and weaker US tariff expectations.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Down about 7% over the past month, mostly on AI equity volatility and positioning, not physical loosening.
Unchanged, 13% above spot. Downside to about $14,600/t at current positioning and about $14,500/t if US stockbuilding stops.
Record high, reflecting tight metal availability in China and outside the US.
Limited near-term tariff expectations, which puts the US stockbuilding assumption at risk.

risk_factors: Copper positioning stays at current levels, which implies a 2027 average of about $14,600/t versus the $15,400/t forecast.
Equity markets price an earlier turn in the AI capex cycle, keeping copper positioning subdued.
US stockbuilding stops, implying a 2027 average of about $14,500/t, with further downside if US inventories flow back to the rest of the world.
Data center moratoria delay projects. The impact is limited through 2028 but larger from 2029, when the forecast relies on projects not yet under construction.
Tariff expectations stay low, or tariffs are rolled back, which weakens the case for US stockbuilding.

vol_and_positioning: Combined COMEX and LME net length is about 9% of open interest as of last week, from about 21% at end-September, below the 16% GS assumes from 2027.
Copper has tracked the GS AI Data Center basket since late 2025, so copper positioning is tied to AI equity sentiment.
The COMEX-LME spread implies a duty of 1% for January 2027 and about 6-7% for January 2028.
geopolitical: US midterm elections produced a Democratic sweep, which GS ties to AI equity volatility and to data center moratoria and tariff policy risk.
Democratic governors in Texas, Georgia and Michigan are expected to impose short-lived, conditional data center moratoria, and the Texas governor-elect has called for an immediate moratorium.
US tariffs on refined copper remain a presidential decision under Section 232, and a legislative rollback would need bipartisan support.
China's scrap shortage and a limited metal supply in China and outside the US are cited as tightening forces.

tension_points.bull_case: Physical fundamentals remain tight: the Yangshan import premium is at a record above $200/t, ex-US inventories are near seasonal lows, and GS holds a $15,400/t 2027 forecast with 13% upside.
tension_points.bear_case: Positioning has dropped to about 9% of open interest versus the 16% assumed, implying about $14,600/t. If US stockbuilding stops, the average falls to about $14,500/t as tariff expectations fade.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Net length staying near 9% of open interest, or US stockbuilding stopping altogether, would undercut the $15,400/t 2027 forecast.

theme_stances.key_argument: Physical fundamentals remain tight and the recent correction is positioning-driven, but AI-related positioning and weaker US tariff expectations are downside risks to the forecast.
theme_stances.evidence: We see the recent correction as positioning-driven rather than reflecting loosening fundamentals.
